edits.value_json: A source reports 大 meaning “big,” opposite 小, in a bronze inscription; the reported example does not establish the earliest attestation.

The whole graph is interpreted as a frontal human figure; whether its arms hang down or extend outward is disputed. Some accounts identify the figure as an adult, a proposed interpretation rather than a settled original sense.
Read the whole graph as a frontal human figure, not as smaller signs. Some accounts interpret it as an adult; the figure’s pose is disputed.

An Eastern Han dictionary account gives 大 as an ancient form of 亣. A later commentary treats them as one character with slightly different shapes, later placed in separate sections; this lexicographic account does not establish prehistoric origin.
